title: On Withdrawing the charge before the hearing
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：withdraw　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 withdraw 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the grandmother ① withdrew the charge before the hearing in the rain, and every child in the courtyard said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the grandmother ② withdraws the charge before the hearing without complaint without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ withdraw the charge before the hearing at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ withdrawn the charge before the hearing before — a line in the diary for February 1950 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Withdrawing the charge before the hearing in the rain, the grandmother said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lamp at the far window, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ withdraw from the school at Easter without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Withdraw from the school at Easter at once and never mention it again.

By 1963 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the diary, and a new child from the next courtyard ⑧ withdraws from the school at Easter in the rain every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the window, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ withdrew the charge before the hearing again when nobody else would.

⑩ To withdraw the charge before the hearing, my mother said in 1968, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the courtyard remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the courtyard forgets, somebody withdraws the charge before the hearing without complaint again and somebody must withdraw the charge before the hearing in the rain all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 撤回（一般过去式 withdrew the charge before the hearing：1956 年祖母头一回这样做，淋着雨）
B. v. 撤回（一般现在 withdraws the charge before the hearing：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 撤回（不定式 to withdraw the charge before the hearing：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 撤回（过去完成时 had withdrawn the charge before the hearing：1950 年二月的日记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 撤回（动名词 withdrawing the charge before the hearing 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 退出（withdraw from the school at Easter：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去退出复活节时从学堂退了学）
G. v. 退出（withdraw from the school at Easter：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 撤回（后段两处：新来的孩子照例 withdraws from the school at Easter，而母亲又一次 withdrew the charge before the hearing）

answers.why: withdraw 意为“撤回”，1956 年祖母淋着雨撤回在开庭前撤回那项指控，那是院子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 withdrew。
withdraw 意为“撤回”，自那以后祖母毫无怨言地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 withdraws。
withdraw 意为“撤回”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯撤回在开庭前撤回那项指控”，此处为不定式 to withdraw the charge before the hearing。
withdraw 意为“撤回”，日记里 二月 那行字说明早在 1963 年之前就有人撤回过，故用过去完成时 had withdrawn。
withdraw 意为“撤回”，祖母说“撤回在开庭前撤回那项指控这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 withdrawing the charge before the hearing 作主语。
withdraw 意为“退出”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去退出复活节时从学堂退了学”，should ever 之后用原形 withdraw from the school at Easter。
withdraw 意为“退出”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻退出复活节时从学堂退了学（withdraw from the school at Easter at once），以后再也不要提起。
withdraw 意为“撤回”，新来的孩子每个年头都照例退出复活节时从学堂退了学，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 withdraws。
withdraw 意为“撤回”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次淋着雨撤回在开庭前撤回那项指控，用一般过去式 withdrew 叙述。
withdraw 意为“撤回”，结尾那句是母亲 1968 年的话：要撤回在开庭前撤回那项指控，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和院子记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 withdraw 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1956 the grandmother withdrew the charge before the hearing in the rain, and nobody in the courtyard forgot it.
Even now the grandmother withdraws the charge before the hearing without complaint whenever the courtyard asks.
Withdrawing the charge before the hearing in the rain, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever withdraw from the school at Easter without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new child from the next courtyard withdraws from the school at Easter in the rain every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother withdrew the charge before the hearing again, and the courtyard remembered that half.
